features.summary: Firefox replaced its old online Web Speech recognition path with local, on-device recognition based on the Parakeet engine, the HWInference process, and downloadable models managed through ModelHub. The Web Speech API now has more complete standards behavior, including locale-based model selection, `continuous` recognition, model availability and installation, permission prompts with download progress, AI Controls and Permissions Policy checks, and accurate result, confidence, timing, stop, and abort events. The tests now verify how Firefox handles WebM initialization segments placed back to back, while expected AbortError messages from tearing down media tests are handled quietly when cleanup interrupts a pending play() promise. _These changes mainly improve correctness checks and test stability rather than changing what users see._

This ensures subtitle/caption event callbacks run in a safe, well-defined context and reduces subtle stability or security issues in the captions pipeline.
